questions.q: A transistor is connected in common-emitter (CE) configuration. The collector supply is $8 \mathrm{~V}$ and the voltage drop across a resistor is $500 \Omega$ in the collector circuit is $0.6 \mathrm{~V}$. If the current gain factor $\alpha$ is $0.96$, find the base current
questions.solution:
Given, $V_{C C}=8 \mathrm{~V}$
Voltage drop, $V_0=\Delta I_C R_L=0.6 \mathrm{~V}$
Load Resistor, $R_L=500 \Omega$
Gain factor, $\alpha=0.96\because \quad \beta=\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}=\frac{0.96}{1-0.96}=24$
Now, $\quad V_0=\Delta I_C R_L0.6=\Delta I_C \times 500\Delta I_C=\frac{0.6}{500}=1.2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~A}$
Now,
$\beta=\frac{\Delta I_C}{\Delta I_B}\therefore$ Base current $\Delta I_B=\frac{\Delta I_C}{\beta}=\frac{1.2 \times 10^{-3}}{24}=5 \times 10^{-5}=50 \times 10^{-6}\Delta I_B=50 \mu \mathrm{A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A zener diode of voltage $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{Z}}(=6 \mathrm{~V})$ is used to maintain a constant voltage across a load resistance $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{L}}(=1000 \Omega)$ by using a series resistance $R_{\mathrm{s}}(=100 \Omega)$. If the e.m.f. of source is $\mathrm{E}(=9 \mathrm{~V})$, what is the power being dissipated in Zener diode?
questions.solution:
Here, $E=9 \mathrm{~V} ; \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{z}}=6 ; \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{L}}=1000 \Omega$ and $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{s}}=100 \Omega$,

Potential drop across series resistor $\mathrm{V}=\mathrm{E}-\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{Z}}=9-6=3 \mathrm{~V}$

Current through series resistance $R_{S}$ is $\mathrm{I}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{R}}=\frac{3}{100}=0.03 \mathrm{~A}$

Current through load resistance $R_{L}$ is $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{L}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{Z}}}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{L}}}=\frac{6}{1000}=0.006 \mathrm{~A}$

Current through Zener diode is $\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{Z}}=\mathrm{I}-\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{L}}=0.03-0.006=0.024 \mathrm{amp} .$ Power dissipated in Zener diode is $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{Z}}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{Z}} \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{Z}}=6 \times 0.024=0.144 \mathrm{Watt}$

If the temperature of the semiconductor is raised.

This will increase the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> and as a result the rate of collision of charge carriers will increase. This will decrease the drift speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math>.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a CE transistor amplifier, the audio signal voltage across the collector resistance of $2.0 \mathrm{k} \Omega$ is $2.0 \mathrm{~V}$. Suppose the current amplification factor of the transistor is 100 , What should be the value of $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{B}}$ in series with $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{BB}}$ supply of $2.0 \mathrm{~V}$ if the dc base current has to be 10 times the signal current?
questions.solution:
The output ac voltage is $2.0 \mathrm{~V}$. So, the ac collector current $\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{C}}=2.0 / 2000=1.0 \mathrm{~mA}$.

The signal current through the base is, therefore given by $\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{i}_{\mathrm{C}} / \beta=1.0 \mathrm{~mA} / 100=0.010 \mathrm{~mA}$

The dc base current has to be $10 \times 0.010=0.10 \mathrm{~mA}$

\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{B}}=\left(\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{BB}}-\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{BE}}\right) / \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{B}}



Assuming $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{BE}}=0.6 \mathrm{~V}, \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{B}}=(2.0 .0 .6) / 0.10=14 \mathrm{k} \Omega$
